hallucinations.claim: "the 2026 exemption of $12.92 million per person"
hallucinations.why: The 2026 federal exemption is $15 million (One Big Beautiful Bill Act). $12.92M was the 2023 figure, a stale number presented as current. This is a sheet trap.

hallucinations.claim: "Brazil has no inheritance tax on those foreign-origin assets"
hallucinations.why: This is unsettled, not a fact. STF (2021) blocked state taxation of foreign inheritances pending a complementary law, but EC 132/2023 lets states tax them meanwhile, so a Brazilian tax resident's US accounts may face ITCMD claims.

hallucinations.claim: "If you die without a Brazilian will, forced-heirship rules apply"
hallucinations.why: Wrong. Forced heirship (50% reserved for necessary heirs) applies to the Brazilian estate whether or not there is a will. A will can dispose of only the other half.

hallucinations.claim: "ITBI ... a transfer tax paid by the inheritor when the title is transferred"
hallucinations.why: Wrong. ITBI is the municipal tax on onerous inter-vivos transfers. Transfers on death are taxed by the state ITCMD, not ITBI.

hallucinations.claim: "If the aggregate value of all foreign assets exceeds $10,000, they must file a FBAR (FinCEN 114). FATCA reporting (Form 8938) may also be required" for the inherited apartment
hallucinations.why: FBAR covers foreign financial accounts, not directly held real estate. Form 8938 also excludes directly held foreign real estate.

hallucinations.claim: "Florianópolis rates are lower, around 4 %"
hallucinations.why: ITCMD is a state tax (Santa Catarina), not a city rate. SC's is progressive, about 1-7% after Lei 19.053/2024, not a flat 4%.

hallucinations.claim: "The transfer is a taxable event for that beneficiary" (401k/IRA)
hallucinations.why: Inheriting a retirement account is not itself a taxable event. Distributions are taxed as income when withdrawn (subject to the 10-year rule), which is imprecise for a finance-literate asker.

hallucinations.claim: "Heirs who receive the apartment must also report it on their U.S. tax returns"
hallucinations.why: A bequest from a US-citizen decedent is not reportable income to US heirs, and there is no general reporting duty for inherited foreign real estate held directly.

what_went_wrong: The gpt-oss:20b merge stated model-knowledge errors as fact: a stale estate-tax exemption, a confused ITBI/ITCMD split, forced heirship tied to having no will, and FBAR on real estate. The decent law-firm search results (brazilcounsel, Martin Law) were not used for the 50% forced share or the ITCMD-on-foreign-assets question.
great_answer_would: Lead with the apartment: Brazilian law, a 50% forced share regardless of will, inventário, and SC ITCMD of about 1-7%. Then cover the US accounts: beneficiary/TOD, the $15M 2026 exemption, and the unsettled Brazilian claim on foreign assets after EC 132. Close with a three-item plan: a Brazilian will, beneficiary designations, and a Brazilian estate lawyer before buying.
notes: Correct pieces: US accounts pass by beneficiary designation or US probate, US estate tax on a citizen's worldwide estate, the apartment goes through inventário, the 8% ITCMD ceiling. Most of the specific numbers and rules beyond that are wrong. It assumes the US accounts are 401(k)/IRA without saying so. It closes with an 'In short' recap that Pat asked to skip.
